subject: performance cost of extra transformed parameters?

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: performance cost of extra transformed parameters?
parts:
Hi!

I was wondering what the cost (performance wise) is when declaring in the transformed parameters block extra variables which can be avoided. For example, consider a population model where I have a couple of random effects and I code these using the Matt trick. Then I end up with defining in the parameter block the "raw" variables

parameters {
   ...
   vector[E] omega; // scales
   matrix[E,J] xi;  // raw values
}

and I often tend to just define in the tranformed parameters block

transformed parameters {
    matrix[E,J] eta;

   eta <- diag_pre_multiply(omega, xi);

    ... compute stuff with eta for the log-lik ...
}

Having eta in the output is convenient, but not necessary. I mean, I could place the computations with eta inside of a local block in the transformed parameters block and then generate them again in the generated quantities block.

So, is it worth the effort to calculate stuff twice (local block in tranformed parameters & generated quantities to output it)? Or would you advise to place the eta stuff in the model block which anyway does not store declared variables. I am asking because I wonder what is best performance wise, i.e. what reduces the burden for the autodiff stack of Stan during sampling?

Many thanks!

Best,
Sebastian

BTW, is the diag_pre_multiply the best way to achieve this operation or is there an even faster operation?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: performance cost of extra transformed parameters?
parts:
On Wednesday, July 8, 2015 at 4:28:57 AM UTC-4, Sebastian Weber wrote:
So, is it worth the effort to calculate stuff twice (local block in tranformed parameters & generated quantities to output it)? Or would you advise to place the eta stuff in the model block which anyway does not store declared variables. I am asking because I wonder what is best performance wise, i.e. what reduces the burden for the autodiff stack of Stan during sampling?

Whether you put something in transformed parameters or the model block has the same implication for autodiff (and autodiff is not used in generated quantities). So, really the only way that there could be a noticeable performance implication is if the validation check --- which is performed for transformed parameters but not in the model or generated quantities blocks --- is expensive. But the only expensive one is the positive definiteness check, and that can be avoided if you know a matrix is positive definite by construction by declaring it as a plain square matrix rather than a covariance matrix.

The diag_pre_multiply() function, on the other hand, is designed to avoid putting unnecessary stuff onto the autodiff stack. It just scales each row of the right-most matrix by the corresponding element of the diagonal vector, rather than multiplying columns by the off-diagonal zeros and summing. So, there isn't a way to do it faster unless the right-most matrix is also structured.

Ben
